newsitem.title: USA: Army Corps of Engineers to repair Calif. levees.
newsitem.headline: Army Corps of Engineers to repair Calif. levees.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson said Wednesday the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers would repair levees broken or damaged by flooding earlier this year.

The Corps of Engineers has agreed to repair levees at several sites along the Feather River and the Bear River in Yuba County, Calif., to their original height and shape as the Republican governor had requested, Wilson's office announced.
The levees on the two northern California rivers were broken or damaged during the January storms.
Levee breaks in California's Central Valley flooded more than 160,000 acres and forced 120,000 people from their homes.

"Repairing and restoring levees to their pre-flood full capacity will ensure a higher degree of protection for the lives, homes, property and businesses of the families who live in these affected areas," Wilson said in a statement.
The Army Corps of Engineers said it would begin pre-flood-level repairs by the end of the month and should complete the work in about four weeks, according to Wilson.
The Army Corps of Engineers estimated that more than 200 miles of levees need repairs before the rainy season returns next fall.
In a February letter to President Clinton, Wilson recommended that the Army Corps of Engineers restore damaged flood control facilities to pre-flood capacity.
